name: Brunelleschi's Dome, Engineering the Renaissance
summary: Filippo Brunelleschi completes the dome of Florence Cathedral (Santa Maria del Fiore), 42 meters diameter, no external buttresses, built without wooden centering using an innovative double-shell herringbone brick technique. Pope Eugenius IV consecrates the cathedral in 1436. The dome, visible from throughout the Tuscan countryside, represents the first great architectural achievement to surpass Roman antiquity.

_quarry.structural_significance: Brunelleschi's dome is the founding monument of Renaissance architecture and Renaissance confidence in human reason overcoming ancient problems; his solution, reinventing Roman engineering techniques from first principles and combining them with new innovations, models the Renaissance approach to classical heritage; the dome's civic significance for Florence (a symbol of the city's wealth, ambition, and technical mastery) demonstrates how architecture functioned as political communication
